title: Tenant-aware traffic mosaicking and safe spillover for model updates
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Problem: During multi-variant model rollouts we observe unsafe spillover when a single region or capacity tier saturates. Current routing sends excess traffic to the next-available variant without taking tenant weights, per-tenant affinity, or per-tenant QoS contracts into account. This causes noisy neighbor effects and customer-visible latency spikes for high-priority tenants.

Goal: Implement tenant-aware traffic mosaicking: a routing layer that composes fractional traffic lanes per-tenant across region and capacity tiers while enforcing tenant SLAs and preserving per-variant KV cache locality to minimize cold-start amplification. The feature should enable safe spillover (gradual redistribution) when capacity saturates, while guaranteeing no high-priority tenant loses more than X% of their baseline throughput during an incident or rollout.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a lightweight tenant profile store that contains: priority (P0-P3), affinity hints (region preferred, KV-cache pinning), and max-spill-percentage. 2) Enhance the routing fabric to compute per-request target lanes by evaluating (tenant_profile, variant_compatibility, region_health, tier_capacity) and choosing a mosaicked path that minimizes cross-tenant disruption. 3) Implement a spillover orchestrator that throttles redistribution using token-bucket rate limits and slow-start ramps backed by feedback from per-tenant p95 latency and cache-miss rate. 4) Provide an emergency dial to pin tenants to their legacy variant for safety and an automated regression detector that triggers rollback when error-rate or hallucination-SLI regressions cross thresholds.

Trade-offs considered: centralizing tenant profiles simplifies decisions but adds a single point of failure; we mitigate with a TTL-backed local cache. Strong affinity for cache locality reduces cold-start but can increase cost; the orchestrator includes a cost budget check to avoid unbounded spend.
acceptance_criteria: Routing layer uses tenant profiles to compute per-request lane with >=95% deterministic matches for identical inputs during tests
During synthetic saturation tests, high-priority tenants (P0/P1) maintain >=90% of baseline throughput while low-priority tenants absorb spillover
Automated regression detector fires rollback when hallucination-score OR p99 latency for any P0 tenant increases beyond configured thresholds
No single region spill triggers global cascade: spill is capped per-tenant by max-spill-percentage and orchestrator enforces backpressure
test_plan: Unit tests for tenant profile read/write and TTL cache semantics
Integration test with canary harness: inject 30% synthetic load on Region-A GPU pool and assert spillover behavior matches policy
Chaos test: kill regional networking to validate failover preserves per-tenant limits and cache-affinity heuristics
E2E perf bench with real workloads (chat and embeddings) measuring p50/p95/p99 latency and KV cache miss rate
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Developer sandbox rollout (internal tenants only) - 1 week
Stage 2: Canary for low-risk tenants (10% traffic, non-P0) - 2 days observation
Stage 3: Expand to mixed tenants (30% traffic) with strict monitoring and gated escalation
Stage 4: Gradual default-on for all new rollouts, opt-in beta for selected existing customers
Manual emergency pin available for customer success to revert tenant to pinned variant in <5 minutes
monitoring_slo: Per-tenant p95 latency <= baseline*1.25 for P0; KV cache cold-start rate delta <= 5% absolute for P0 tenants over 24h window
rollback_criteria: Automated: hallucination-score increase > 3x baseline for any P0 tenant over 1h
Automated: p99 latency increase > 200ms for P0 tenants sustained for 15m
Manual: severity ticket from CS indicating >5% of active sessions impacted for a customer
